objective: Measure parallel speculative decoding on GPT-OSS-20B MXFP4 and explain MoE-specific differences versus previous dense Qwen3-8B results.
baseline: Same SGLang target, identical MXFP4 checkpoint, attention backend, KV budget, graph settings; AR before/after each task/BS group.

inputs.template: Frozen target-native Harmony IDs, medium reasoning; date fixed at 2026-11-06 using the Jinja strftime_now override.

controls_and_limits: Keep load, compilation, warmup and cache flush outside headline timings.
Preserve output token IDs and AR/SD, cross-width, cross-BS divergences.
Fixed output throughput is not task quality or natural-EOS application throughput.

Cross-model dense/MoE comparison confounds architecture, precision, activation count, tokenizer and draft. Use within-model width/BS, measured routing and kernel evidence; do not claim a causal MoE-only speedup delta.
Unique-expert-weight bytes estimated from routed expert union are an access-footprint proxy, not measured HBM bytes.
SM active and Tensor active counters do not alone prove compute bound.
No new GitHub push is authorized by this experiment request.
GPT-OSS mixes sliding-window and full softmax attention; it has no GDN recurrent-state verification cache. The log phrase Hybrid SWA does not mean hybrid linear attention.
GPT-OSS uses medium reasoning while the earlier Qwen3-8B cohort used its original non-thinking prompts; acceptance differences also reflect output/content and draft training, not only MoE sparsity.
stage_order_reason: Establish warmed native FP4 kernel/replay evidence before the long unprofiled benchmark matrix.

additional_diagnostic.purpose: Investigate observed BF16-head AR/SD mismatches at prompt0 token6 and prompt1 token46; preserve headline timings and compare diagnostic outputs to headline.
additional_diagnostic.dependency: native03 admission success and process exit
